assertions.reason: Stable, preview, nightly, and dev identities remain aligned across the shared release-channel source of truth, Cargo bundle metadata, install/uninstall scripts, and release workflow logic. The audited matrix shows each channel keeps its matching Neo Zed display name and dev.neozed-derived app ID without channel mixing, while release automation publishes neozed-named desktop artifacts and maps stable/preview/nightly release tags to the correct channel logic.

evidence.summary: The release identity mapping pairs Stable/Preview/Nightly/Dev with Neo Zed, Neo Zed Preview, Neo Zed Nightly, and Neo Zed Dev plus dev.neozed/dev.neozed.Preview/dev.neozed.Nightly/dev.neozed.Dev.
The bundle metadata blocks use matching channel-specific identifiers and names for Neo Zed, Neo Zed Preview, Neo Zed Nightly, and Neo Zed Dev.
The uninstall script routes stable/preview/nightly/dev through matching app IDs, app bundle names, and db suffixes, preserving per-channel consistency on both Linux and macOS.
Stable releases require v${version} tags and preview releases require v${version}-pre tags, while release_nightly.yml forces the nightly channel before bundling.
Release workflows upload neozed-linux-*.tar.gz, neozed-*.dmg, and neozed-*.exe artifacts for the public desktop releases.
Saved the per-channel matrix and workflow checks to evidence/release-docs/cross-consistency/cross-audit.json.

assertions.reason: The public fork identity tuple — Neo Zed, neozed, neozed://, dev.neozed*, neozed.dev, and https://github.com/Nkr1shna/neo-zed/ — is present across the audited release-facing source-of-truth files, CLI/docs surfaces, scripts, workflows, and checklist/release docs. Scoped conflict checks found no unexpected upstream tuple values in the audited scope; the only remaining legacy values are explicitly documented compatibility holdovers such as accepting zed:// for old deep links and rejecting old dev.zed Flatpak IDs in tests.

evidence.summary: The CLI exposes neozed:// as the public scheme, uses the neozed command throughout help text, and keeps only explicit compatibility aliases/legacy URL acceptance where documented.
The docs theme background noise image and download CTA now use Neo Zed-owned https://neozed.dev paths.
The checklist records the full Neo Zed identity tuple, the fork repository URL, and the intentionally preserved compatibility holdovers.
The telemetry doc points to the fork repository and hi@neozed.dev, reinforcing the public Neo Zed web/repo/support tuple in release-facing docs.
Saved tuple-presence checks, allowed compatibility holdovers, and the scoped no-conflict audit to evidence/release-docs/cross-consistency/cross-audit.json.

frictions: Task-based user-testing-flow-validator subagents failed to launch with "Invalid model: custom:droidproxy:gpt-5.4", so these flow reports were produced manually in the validator session using the assigned assertion scopes.
notes: No services or seed data were required for the release-docs milestone.

Allowed compatibility holdovers in the audited scope were limited to legacy zed:// acceptance, a negative test that rejects old dev.zed Flatpak IDs, and the separately documented zed-remote-server artifact names retained for compatibility.
